screening_decisions.reason: This is a mathematical model estimating required sensitivity of POC tests, not a diagnostic accuracy study reporting test performance with 2x2 data.
This is a meta-epidemiological study on publication bias, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a decision analysis focusing on treatment strategies and same-day treatment outcomes, not a diagnostic accuracy study presenting 2x2 data for index vs reference test.

This is a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating the QuickVue test against PCR, reporting sensitivity and specificity (2x2 data) for high and low prevalence populations. Participants were nonpregnant women and men of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is a clinical practice guideline, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a commentary/review on the way forward for STI diagnostics, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

This is a prospective field evaluation of two POC tests (CRT and ACON) compared to NAAT, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were men and women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.

This is a clinic-based evaluation of a rapid test (Clearview Chlamydia MF) versus gold standard (Roche Amplicor CT assay), reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age at high risk, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.

This is a prospective cohort study evaluating a rapid urine test for chlamydia in men versus PCR, reporting sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV (2x2 data). Participants were men of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is a set of recommendations for laboratory-based detection, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a systematic review of point-of-care testing, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a summary of evidence reviewed for treatment guidelines, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a comparative effectiveness and cost-effectiveness analysis using decision modeling, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

This evaluates a home-based Chlamydia test (HandiLab-C) versus NAAT, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is about treatment of Haemophilus ducreyi infection, not diagnostic accuracy.
This describes a tool for quality assessment of diagnostic accuracy studies (QUADAS-2), not a diagnostic accuracy study itself.
This is about bivariate analysis methods for diagnostic reviews, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a systematic review of point-of-care tests, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
This is about partner notification effects, not diagnostic accuracy.

This evaluates the performance of Chlamydia rapid tests (Clearview MF and CRT) versus PCR in resource-limited settings, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age (low- and high-risk), enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This assesses the performance of tests for publication bias in systematic reviews of diagnostic test accuracy, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
This is an interpretation of findings from randomized controlled trials on screening and treatment to prevent PID, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is about risk factors for PID among sex workers, not diagnostic accuracy.
This is about applying GRADE to make evidence-based recommendations about diagnostic tests, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a review of current methods of laboratory diagnosis, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a systematic review of clinical effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of rapid point-of-care tests, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a systematic review of noninvasive testing for chlamydial and gonococcal infections, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

This evaluates the Biostar Chlamydia OIA assay versus cell culture, DFA, and PCR, reporting relative sensitivities (2x2 data). Participants were women of reproductive age attending an STD clinic, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is a population-based prevalence survey of STIs, not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating a specific index test versus reference standard.

This is a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating rapid tests for CT, NG, and syphilis in symptomatic women versus NAAT, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age with symptoms, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.

This compares different assays (PACE 2, amplification assays, Clearview EIA) for detection of Chlamydia trachomatis, reporting sensitivities with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.

This evaluates the BioStar Chlamydia OIA in adolescent women versus NAAT, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.

This is a pilot study evaluating the Chlamydia Rapid Test Device versus PCR in asymptomatic men, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were men of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is a prevalence study using PCR to detect Chlamydia trachomatis, not evaluating a specific index test versus reference standard.
This is a review of laboratory diagnosis of Chlamydia trachomatis infections, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is sentinel surveillance of STIs/HIV and risk behaviors, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is about prevalence and factors associated with infections in symptomatic women, not evaluating a specific index test versus reference standard.

This evaluates a rapid point-of-care test for Chlamydia trachomatis in specimens from sex workers versus PCR, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is a review article describing various tests for chlamydial and gonorrheal infections, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

This evaluates a new Chlamydia Rapid Test versus PCR and strand displacement amplification assays, reporting sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV (2x2 data). Participants were women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is an analysis of Chlamydia trachomatis serovars and their association with clinical manifestations, not a diagnostic accuracy study.

This evaluates the Chlamydia Rapid Test (CRT) versus NAAT in two clinics in Suriname, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is about immune response modulation mechanisms induced by Chlamydia trachomatis associated with infertility, not diagnostic accuracy.
This is about search strategies to identify diagnostic accuracy studies, not a diagnostic accuracy study itself.

This evaluates a rapid assay (OIA) for detection of Chlamydia trachomatis versus LCR, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.

This evaluates three POC tests (Handilab-C, Biorapid CHLAMYDIA Ag test, QuickVue Chlamydia test) versus NAAT, reporting sensitivities with 2x2 data. Participants were women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
This is a discussion of risk factors for genital chlamydial infection, not a diagnostic accuracy study.
This is a set of guidelines for laboratory diagnosis of Chlamydia trachomatis infections in East European countries, not a diagnostic accuracy study.

This evaluates a new prototype POC Chlamydia test versus NAAT, reporting sensitivity and specificity with 2x2 data. Participants were adolescent women of reproductive age, enrolled consecutively, and all received index and reference tests.
